title: Predator–Prey and the Pendulum
short: Study classic nonlinear models in the phase plane.

blocks.html: Two classic nonlinear systems show what linearization can and cannot tell us: rabbits and foxes, and a swinging pendulum.

Lotka–Volterra: $x' = x(a - by)$ (prey), $y' = y(-c + dx)$ (predators). Coexistence equilibrium $\left(\frac{c}{d}, \frac{a}{b}\right)$; its linearization is a center with angular frequency $\sqrt{ac}$, and the populations cycle on closed orbits.
Pendulum: $\theta'' + \frac{g}{L}\sin\theta = 0$, or $\theta' = \omega$, $\omega' = -\frac{g}{L}\sin\theta$. Hanging down $(0, 0)$ is a center (a spiral sink with damping); balanced upright $(\pi, 0)$ is a saddle. Small swings have period $2\pi\sqrt{L/g}$.

For Lotka–Volterra, $J = \begin{bmatrix} a - by & -bx \\ dy & -c + dx \end{bmatrix}$; at $\left(\frac{c}{d}, \frac{a}{b}\right)$ the diagonal vanishes and $J = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -\frac{bc}{d} \\ \frac{ad}{b} & 0 \end{bmatrix}$, with eigenvalues $\pm i\sqrt{ac}$. A center alone is inconclusive, but this model has a conserved quantity, $dx - c\ln x + by - a\ln y$, constant along trajectories, so the orbits are closed. For the pendulum, $J = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -\frac{g}{L}\cos\theta & 0 \end{bmatrix}$; at $\theta = \pi$, $\cos\theta = -1$ gives $\Delta < 0$, a saddle.

blocks.title: Coexistence
blocks.q: Find the coexistence equilibrium of $x' = x(2 - 0.5y)$, $y' = y(-3 + 0.25x)$.

blocks.title: The cycle's period
blocks.q: For that model, estimate the period of small oscillations around $(12, 4)$.

blocks.title: A damped pendulum
blocks.a: hanging down: spiral sink (it swings and settles); upright: saddle (unstable)

blocks.html: Concluding from a linear center that a nonlinear system cycles, or that it does not. For Lotka–Volterra the closed orbits come from the conserved quantity, not from the linearization; add a little crowding term to the prey and the center becomes a spiral sink.

blocks.name: phaseplane
blocks.cap: Lotka–Volterra trajectories are closed loops around $(12, 4)$: prey rise, then predators rise, then prey fall, then predators fall. Press Run and watch the time strip: the predator peaks lag the prey peaks.

blocks.name: phaseplane
blocks.cap: A damped pendulum ($x = \theta$, $y = \omega$). Swings spiral into the hanging positions $\theta = 0, \pm 2\pi$; the saddles at $\theta = \pm\pi$ separate swings that go over the top from those that do not.
